title: The Story of a Mother

full_text:
A mother sat watching by the cradle of her sick child, her heart heavy with dread. A faint knock sounded at the door, and an old man wrapped in a black horse-cloth entered, shivering with cold. It was Death.

While the exhausted mother closed her eyes for a single heartbeat, Death seized the child and fled into the freezing night.

The mother rushed out into the snow, weeping in despair. By the crossroads stood a dark Thorn Bush covered with ice: "I know which way Death went, but I will not tell you unless you warm me against your bosom!" The mother embraced the frozen thorns with all her strength; the sharp spikes pierced her breast, and warm drops of her blood fell upon the twigs. Fresh green leaves and fragrant roses burst forth in the snow, and the Bush pointed the way.

She reached a great, deep Lake that had no boat. The Lake said: "Weep your eyes into my depths; I collect pearls, and I will carry you across!" The mother wept with such boundless sorrow that her two eyes fell into the water like precious gems, and the Lake lifted her like a wave to the opposite shore.

There stood the vast Greenhouse of Death, where millions of living flowers and trees represented the lives of mortals on earth. A withered old woman who guarded the portal said: "Give me your long black hair, and I will let you in!" The mother gladly sheared her raven locks, took the old woman's white hair in return, and searched the greenhouse.

Listening to the heartbeats of the flowers, she recognized the tiny, fluttering pulse of her child in a little blue crocus.

Death entered: "How came you here before me?"
"I am a mother!" she cried.

Death showed her two future lives in the water: one radiant with blessing, and the other tormented by incurable agony and crime. "One of these fates belonged to your child," whispered Death gently. "Would you sentence him to torment?"

The mother fell upon her knees, clasped her hands, and bowed her head in sacred reverence: "Thy will be done, O Lord! Take my child into Thy eternal peace!" And Death bore the innocent soul upward into the everlasting joy of heaven.
moral: A mother's love is stronger than the grave, yet highest faith surrenders all to the divine wisdom of eternity.
